theorem.statement: Every explicit instance \(I\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\) whose underlying full graph \(G\) has exactly one global simple cycle satisfies the hypotheses of \(\texttt{thm:relevant-component-polynomial-frontier}\); hence \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\) gives it a sound-and-complete polynomial-size certificate calculus and a polynomial-time exact decision and optimization algorithm.
theorem.proof_tex: Let \(K\) be any weak component of the underlying undirected full graph, and choose a spanning tree \(T_K\) of \(K\).  Each edge in \(E(K)\setminus E(T_K)\), together with the unique path in \(T_K\) between its endpoints, determines a distinct simple cycle.  Because \(G\) has exactly one global simple cycle, \(|E(K)\setminus E(T_K)|\le 1\), so the cycle rank of every weak component \(K\) is at most one.  In particular, the weak components containing \(X\) and \(Y\) are either distinct, or they coincide in a component of cycle rank at most one.  These are precisely the alternatives in \(\texttt{thm:relevant-component-polynomial-frontier}\), whose conclusion gives the asserted certificate calculus and exact polynomial-time decision and optimization algorithm.

statement_notes.justification: This corollary closes the global-one-cycle question by a direct containment argument without duplicating the stronger relevant-component theorem.
statement_notes.gap: The former open question reduces to verifying that one global simple cycle forces every weak component to have cycle rank at most one.
statement_notes.consumer: The explicit-support backend may dispatch every global-unicycle input directly to \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\).
